races.name: Prestige Safety Your Trusted Safety Partner Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Further Measure
runners_data.note: Proven course-and-distance winner (1W at 16f/STA) who handles this surface well and has the prominent style to sit directly behind Desert Belle; nine-year-old but in form, though T14 blank from three runs is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Glenna
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly stepping up significantly in trip to 1m6f after running 1m-1m2f; has the prominent style to be involved early but the distance extension and switch to Fibresand from softer ground are untested risks.

runners_data.name: Easwrith Destiny
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with only three career starts, all on softer ground and shorter trips; this is a significant step into the unknown over 1m6f on AW, but her lightly-raced profile and trainer David Menuisier's ability to place horses make her intriguing.

runners_data.name: Desert Belle
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner here for Sir Mark Prescott, whose 7/21 T14 strike rate underlines live form; five runs all on Standard AW with a win at 12f/STA and consistent placed efforts — step to 1m6f is the only open question, but the stable rarely runs horses out of range.

runners_data.name: Flash Kozo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best AW effort was a third at 11f/STA; has shown a tendency to finish mid-pack and the Harry Eustace yard has a 2/16 T14 rate — needs a lot to go right at this trip and in this field.

runners_data.name: Tenison
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on soft and has soft-ground form at shorter trips, but is a genuine hold-up horse racing in a position further forward than natural due to the field composition; the "fades in finish" flag and STYLE_FIT of 0.92 suggest treating its chances with caution in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Wave Power
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose best result was a third at 8f/HEA; at 1m6f on Fibresand with no proven form at this trip or surface, the STYLE_FIT discount applies and it would need an unusually strong pace to close effectively from where it will realistically race.

runners_data.name: Victors Spirit
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up performer with multiple Southwell wins and placed efforts at 10-12f/STA; the most credible of the rear-division runners in terms of course aptitude, though 142lbs is a significant burden and 22 days since last run is manageable.

runners_data.name: Marbuzet
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer with excellent 2m-plus grass form (1W2P at 16f/GOO), but the switch to Fibresand and the step down in surface quality from good ground is unproven; Tim Easterby's 8/86 T14 rate is solid and Kirrane is a capable booking.

runners_data.name: It's Only Fun
runners_data.note: Ran prominently in its headgear at 11f/STA for a win and has a P-style note in its headgear record, so may be closer to the pace than its hold-up tag suggests; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers expectations, but 1m6f is the longest trip attempted and stamina is unconfirmed.

races.paceDynamic: Desert Belle is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Luke Morris in the saddle for Sir Mark Prescott, will stride out from the gates over 1m6f on Standard Fibresand and attempt to control tempo from the front without being seriously pressured. Further Measure and Glenna will look to sit prominent in the slipstream, creating a compact lead group that sets a sustainable, even gallop rather than a breakneck pace. The extended distance and standard going suit a patient leader who can conserve energy and dictate terms, making this a race that strongly favours horses capable of sitting within two lengths of Desert Belle and producing a sustained finishing effort — prominent racers with proven stamina at this trip have the clearest tactical advantage. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate: Tenison, It's Only Fun, and Wave Power are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice they are unlikely to secure a truly positive position and face a stiff test of their ability to land a blow from off the pace against a well-controlled gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Desert Belle Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Belle leads uncontested, sets a measured pace, and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Desert Belle controls from the front at a comfortable gallop, with Further Measure and Glenna unable to reel her in from a prominent position; the steady tempo means closers never generate the momentum needed to peg back a fresh leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Further Measure or Glenna track Desert Belle closely and produce a sustained late surge to nail her close home.
scenarios.body: Desert Belle's lead is pegged back in the final furlong by one of the prominent duo who have conserved energy sitting just off the pace; Further Measure's course form and winning run over this course and distance make him a live threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften up the leaders and a hold-up runner finds clear daylight to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Victors Spirit is the most credible of the genuine hold-up types, with proven Southwell form and course-distance experience; however this scenario is tempered by the fact that Tenison, Wave Power and It's Only Fun are redistributed out of their natural position and unlikely to deliver the late burst needed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Belle goes too fast for conditions and the field strings out, leaving a progressive or unexposed stayer to emerge from midfield.
scenarios.body: Marbuzet has strong form over 2m-plus trips on good ground and may find this surface and steady-to-moderate pace less ideal; Easwrith Destiny, lightly raced and stepping up in trip, is the most unexposed runner and could outperform expectations if the race develops slowly.

watchPoints.text: Desert Belle's ability to get the 1m6f trip is the race's single biggest swing factor — if she ties up in the final quarter-mile, Further Measure and Glenna are perfectly placed to capitalise.
Further Measure's headgear note (p) and nine-year-old age mean his prominent position needs to be confirmed at the start; if he drops back early, the pace picture thins considerably.
Glenna's trip extension from 1m2f to 1m6f is a major unknown — watch for signs of greenness or fading after the turn, which would eliminate the most likely challenger to Desert Belle.

Victors Spirit carries top weight of 142lbs alongside Marbuzet — monitor in-running to see whether either hold-up runner can find cover and make smooth headway turning for home, as that is the clearest sign the scenario of a hold-up winner is live.

With three horses (Tenison, Wave Power, It's Only Fun) redistributed out of their natural hold-up role into midfield on the map, watch the early positioning closely — if any manage to get further back than expected, they may have marginally more chance than their STYLE_FIT scores imply.

races.name: Prestige Safety First Aid Training Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Turret
runners_data.note: Balding has him fit after 48 days off (form: 01 on turf) and McDonald takes the ride; genuine pace-setter who will want to roll along from the front, though his single Southwell turf sim-going run produced no win or place — his front-running role here is his strength and biggest asset.

runners_data.name: Crack of Thunder
runners_data.note: Jack Jones yard in quiet form (0/15 over 14 days) and the horse has faded in his last three finishes including a distant eighth over course and distance; a genuine stay-back type who will be squeezed into midfield by the volume of closers in this field, limiting his ability to produce his natural run.

runners_data.name: Argenteus
runners_data.note: Menuisier sends him here on the back of a single run (seventh on Good ground at 12f), stepping him up to AW Fibresand — genuine hold-up horse but his one career start tells us little, and being compressed into midfield rather than his preferred rear position adds positional uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Centrum
runners_data.note: Gosden yard active (8/15 in 14 days), headgear flagged, 48 days off and his only run was an eighth on Soft at 10f — he finishes fades to finish and the step up in trip and switch to AW sand is a significant unknown; mapped to midfield as a displaced closer, not a natural forwardly-placed horse.

runners_data.name: Eshowe
runners_data.note: 231 days off the track is a stark fitness query for Edward Smyth-Osbourne's filly, whose only Southwell run produced a 12th; the headgear flag and long break make her hard to trust, and as a confirmed fader she brings stop-start form into a race where her hold-up style is compromised by field size.

runners_data.name: Humphrey
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (single run, second on Good at 10f for Gosden/Havlin), so the style is genuinely unknown — the unknown tag means punters should allow for any position, and Havlin is an astute handler of green horses who may steal a quiet run through the midfield.

runners_data.name: Kokbastau
runners_data.note: Varian's three-year-old has placed twice in three starts (third and sixth most recently), handles Good going well and steps onto AW Fibresand for the first time; Ray Dawson takes over and the horse looks like a genuine closer who may actually sit where he wants to in this race.

runners_data.name: Sandpyper
runners_data.note: Frost yard's horse has a pattern of fading (tenth last time at Southwell over 11f on Standard), and at 61 days off his fitness is marginally tested; the true hold-up profile is squeezed into midfield here, and his finishing record gives little encouragement for a late burst.

runners_data.name: Hello Friend
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's lightly-raced filly ran back-to-back seconds at 12f (Good and Standard), including a Southwell run — sim-going form confirms she handles AW Fibresand; Sam James picks up the ride and her consistent placed form at today's distance makes her one of the most course-relevant hold-up types in the field.

runners_data.name: Marianita
runners_data.note: Beckett's three-year-old was fourth at 10f on Good then 11th at Southwell over 11f last time, suggesting the AW doesn't entirely suit; 19 days between runs keeps her fit, Hector Crouch partners her, and the fading pattern in her recent finishes is a concern for a hold-up horse in this shape.

runners_data.name: Alfred Wincham
runners_data.note: Patrick Neville's four-year-old boasts two wins from two starts (12f and 18f, both Good ground) and a 7lb claimer Pietropaolo takes the ride; the prominent style suits the position he can realistically secure here, though the switch from Good turf to AW Fibresand is an untested jump.

runners_data.name: Sharp Move
runners_data.note: Haggas and Marquand is a quality combination, and Sharp Move has a win on Standard AW at 10f plus a placed run on Soft — 249 days off the track is a significant question mark, but the prominent style and course-relevant form make him one of the more interesting profiles in this field.

runners_data.name: Bankatary
runners_data.note: Luke Morris partners this James Owen four-year-old who has placed at 16f twice and won at 16f on Good — dropping in trip to 12f suits a prominent galloper who stays, though all three recent runs came on Good and the AW surface is unproven.

runners_data.name: Pic N Mix
runners_data.note: Nick Littmoden's five-year-old has six recent runs all on Good or Soft at 16f with finishes of sixth, seventh, sixth, seven — consistently moderate at longer trips; dropping to 12f on AW Fibresand is a marked change of conditions and his form gives no grounds for optimism in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Turret is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push him along, he is expected to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over the 1m4f Southwell Fibresand trip at standard going. Alfred Wincham, Sharp Move and Bankatary are all prominent types who will track up behind him, creating a small cluster near the head of affairs but without the aggression to seriously disrupt Turret's rhythm. The large contingent of natural hold-up horses — Crack of Thunder, Eshowe, Centrum, Argenteus, Kokbastau, Sandpyper, Marianita and Pic N Mix — cannot all find genuine rearward positions and several will be shuffled into midfield whether they like it or not, blurring the tactical picture in the pack. Turret holds more than can all get their natural position: of the prominent types, Turret himself, Alfred Wincham and Sharp Move are best placed to actually control the early order; with a sustainable, uncontested pace from the front, this race shape decisively favours patient prominent racers and the sharpest of the hold-up types who can travel comfortably through midfield and attack a single time in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Turret Controls, Prominent Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Turret bowls along uncontested and the pace remains honest but not brutal, allowing prominent trackers to strike in the straight.
scenarios.body: Turret sets a measured gallop that keeps the field strung out without burning off the chasers, and the prominent types immediately behind him have enough left to pounce when the race quickens two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pick Off Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves just fast enough to drain Turret and the prominent pack, leaving a gap for the sharpest finishers.
scenarios.body: The prominent group hits the straight with energy reserves dwindling and the freshest hold-up types — those actually sitting in midfield positions — cut through to win a slowly-run but physically demanding contest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Heats Up, Front Runs Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster of Alfred Wincham, Sharp Move and Bankatary applies pressure to Turret early, turning this into a genuinely run race.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop filters out the hold-up horses who struggle to sustain and rewards the horse with the best combination of stamina and front-running courage who simply keeps galloping.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Sneaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments into an untidy, traffic-ridden contest where gaps appear late for a horse tracking midfield on the inside.
scenarios.body: A horse who navigates cleanly through the congested pack of displaced hold-up types benefits from a clear run that others miss, arriving late with untapped energy.

watchPoints.text: Turret (McDonald/Balding) has an uncontested lead and any drifting of pace in the final quarter-mile will be the critical trigger — watch whether the prominent pack of Alfred Wincham and Sharp Move closes the gap before the straight or allows him daylight.

The sheer volume of displaced hold-up horses — Crack of Thunder, Centrum, Eshowe, Argenteus, Sandpyper — compressed into midfield creates significant traffic risk in the straight; watch for horses getting blocked or switching wide at the two-furlong pole.

Sharp Move returns from 249 days off for Haggas — if he shows any greenness or sluggishness leaving the stalls, his prominent style will be compromised and he could drop back into the congested midfield group rather than tracking the pace.

Hello Friend's two consecutive seconds over today's trip including a Southwell run make her the most course-and-distance relevant of the hold-up types; watch whether Sam James opts to track midfield or drops her out, as the former is far more dangerous in this race shape.

Alfred Wincham is unbeaten in two starts but both wins came on Good turf — watch how he handles the Fibresand surface in the early furlongs, as any discomfort on the artificial track would rapidly undermine the prominent plan.

races.name: Prestige Safety E-learning @ Prestigesafetyservices.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with an OR of 69, placed twice in six similar-going runs but winless; Hector Crouch takes the ride and 42 days off may mean a fresh, sharpened-up version, though from the rear on a flat track with a modest pace this horse will need everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Roc De Fer
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's horses typically improve with each run and T14 shows 7 winners in 21 runners — a powerful strike rate — but this horse's true style is to come from the back, and in a field where the hold-up positions are congested, getting a clear run will be the challenge.

runners_data.name: Five Moons
runners_data.note: Consistent placer across five recent Southwell/Standard surfaces (five in five) for the Simon & Ed Crisford yard, which is in form (T14: 3/16); a natural hold-up type who will be squeezed into a midfield slot he would not naturally choose in this crowded field, blunting his chance.

runners_data.name: Sun Lord
runners_data.note: Ran creditably in third over 11f on soft ground last time out and steps onto all-weather for the first time; running style is unknown so his tactical position is uncertain, but the trip and surface switch are the key questions Oisin Orr must answer on the day.

runners_data.name: Alkumatic Jo Jo
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here and the horse that sets the pace tone for the entire race; De Sousa has the tools to control fractions, but five of nine starts on similar going have produced only two placed efforts and no wins, so front-running in this company is a slight style stretch (STYLE_FIT 0.93).

runners_data.name: Miss Pretty
runners_data.note: Wore headgear (p) for her win at Southwell over 7f on Standard going earlier in her campaign and should be among the more prominent horses behind the leader; Georgia Dobie is relatively inexperienced but the horse's course form and positive going record (1W1P from 4) make her a natural fit for the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Brave Leader
runners_data.note: Headgear (p) in use and a genuine hold-up horse whose last five runs produced two placed efforts on Standard or Soft ground; Sean Levey rides but the Tom Ward yard is winless in the past 14 days, and being shuffled from his natural rear position into an overcrowded midfield is a meaningful negative.

runners_data.name: Carwyn
runners_data.note: A flagged horse that fades in finishes, with nine poor results from recent starts on Good and Soft and now stepping onto Standard AW; even in midfield this horse carries a strong fade warning, and headgear (p) has not sparked a turnaround.

runners_data.name: Tinsel
runners_data.note: Course winner over 10f on Standard going (1W from 7 on similar surfaces) and PJ McDonald provides stable experience; a natural hold-up type who will be grouped with several others in the midfield pack, meaning a clear passage inside the final furlong is far from guaranteed after 83 days off.

runners_data.name: Seraglio Point
runners_data.note: Shaped promisingly for a placed third at Goodwood and has only three runs to his name, so there is scope for improvement; Tom Marquand is a high-class booking, but with only one similar-going run (third on Standard) there is more unknown here than most rivals.

runners_data.name: Prince Of Calypso
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field at OR 70 alongside Corallience, wearing headgear (p); hold-up style with three placed efforts from limited starts, all on faster ground, and Billy Loughnane must find a clear run from the back on a track that does not always suit late finishers.

runners_data.name: Corallience
runners_data.note: Joint top-rated at OR 70 but shows a modest Southwell record (7th of 10f/STA last time), and David Menuisier's yard has had no winners in the past 14 days; a hold-up horse in headgear who will be operating from the rear of a field stacked with similar types.

runners_data.name: James Choice
runners_data.note: Unknown running style (U) from Warren Greatrex with Edward Greatrex in the saddle — a stable combination — but form string (643-6) reflects little consistency and the one similar-going run produced a sixth; how this horse positions in the early stages is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Won twice in a row on Soft ground and looks progressive (OR 69), but Southwell form shows nothing of note (7th and 8th from two runs) and Hugo Palmer's yard (T14: 3/16) is in decent form; headgear worn and the hold-up style will demand a gap that may not materialise given the crowded midfield.

races.paceDynamic: Alkumatic Jo Jo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 1m3f Southwell handicap and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Silvestre De Sousa should be able to dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop from the outset. The early pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the race into a tactical contest where position and a turn of foot in the straight matter more than relentless galloping. Miss Pretty and Sun Lord are the most natural prominent-running types capable of tracking Alkumatic Jo Jo, while Fans Favourite and Tinsel, both winners on this surface, will need to work their way into contention from further back. The field contains far more hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Roc De Fer, Five Moons, Brave Leader, Carwyn, and Tinsel are true hold-up types pushed into midfield slots they may not naturally find — meaning those shown in midfield are likely to be crowding one another rather than enjoying a clean run. This race shape unambiguously favours horses that can travel prominently off the frugal pace and quicken inside the final two furlongs, with lone-front-runner followers and hold-up types on the outside of the field the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alkumatic Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Alkumatic Jo Jo sets a modest, uncontested pace and De Sousa controls the race from the front throughout.
scenarios.body: Alkumatic Jo Jo idles along in front at a comfortable clip, leaving those racing at the back of the field with too much ground to make up in the short Southwell straight; horses tracking closely into the home bend are perfectly placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Pretty or Sun Lord sit just off Alkumatic Jo Jo's pace and produce a decisive move two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace suits a horse with a tactical turn of foot that has been travelling comfortably in second or third, requiring only a short, sharp burst to put the race to bed; the lack of a strong gallop means the finish is determined by finishing kick rather than stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch the field and leave an opening for a late closer with a clean passage.
scenarios.body: Fans Favourite, a dual recent winner on soft ground but with limited Southwell form, or Tinsel, a course winner, would need a gap to appear in the final furlong and rivals to tire; this scenario is discounted because so many true hold-up horses are compressed into midfield, creating traffic and reducing the likelihood of a clean finishing run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Alkumatic Jo Jo sets a pace that collapses in the straight, causing a scramble among horses caught flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A sudden deceleration reshuffles the race, briefly favouring any horse with energy reserves and a clear run, though the bunched midfield of redistributed hold-up types means clean passages will be scarce; this is the least likely shape given the Standard going and a lone front-runner with a history of in-frame finishes.

watchPoints.text: Alkumatic Jo Jo (De Sousa) controls all the early fractions — watch whether he allows the pace to drift very slowly, which could compress the entire field into the home bend and negate any length advantage for hold-up horses.

The midfield is packed with redistributed hold-up types (Roc De Fer, Five Moons, Brave Leader, Carwyn, Tinsel) — watch for crowding and interference on the home bend as these horses all seek a run simultaneously.

Miss Pretty's headgear (p) and Southwell course win make her dangerous if she travels prominently behind the leader — watch whether Georgia Dobie secures a position on Alkumatic Jo Jo's shoulder from the outset.

Fans Favourite arrives on the back of two wins but both came on Soft ground and Southwell Standard is a different surface test — watch whether Kevin Stott opts for an aggressive ride to offset the style disadvantage.
Sir Mark Prescott's T14 strike rate of 7/21 with Roc De Fer is notable — watch the market for any significant move, as Prescott horses frequently improve sharply when switched to new conditions.

races.name: Prestige Safety Fire Risk Assessments Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Thisonesforyou
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here, and Clive Cox's filly won over this course and distance last time out, giving her strong tactical control; going is suitable but her OR-63 mark at this distance on AW makes retaining that advantage crucial — her chance hinges entirely on how hard the prominent pair press her.

runners_data.name: Kiani King
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over for Hughie Morrison on this 67-day returner, but the horse is a genuine closer pushed into a mapped midfield role given the volume of hold-up types in the field; three of four starts at this track going return respectable positions but no wins, and the long absence is a concern.

runners_data.name: Mehmas Engine
runners_data.note: Luke Dace's gelding carries a headgear flag and a worrying pattern of finishing ninth in both recent Southwell starts, with the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag making it hard to trust even if positioned more forward than usual; a true hold-up horse being shown in midfield due to field congestion, with form that offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Bosom Pals
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's colt won at 7f on Good ground last season and placed twice from hold-up positions, but natural style means he'll be competing for late ground in a field full of identical closers; the 44-day break and AW debut add further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Back At One
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's yard has been in sharp 14-day form (6/16) but this lightly-raced three-year-old has only three starts to his name and is a genuine hold-up horse pushed to midfield on the map; two of three runs at Southwell standard returned mid-table finishes, and the step to 1m is unexplored.

runners_data.name: Topathemorning
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams sends this colt back to Southwell where he finished fifth on his most recent start at the track; a genuine hold-up type who will need a strong pace to reel in the front-runners, and with only one sim-going run from three returning a placing, he remains unproven at this level.

runners_data.name: Sagremor
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's colt has placed over 8f on soft and has a headgear flag; a true closer who has struggled at Southwell (5th, 8th in sim-going outings) and the 66-day layoff combined with Sean Levey's familiarity with the track represents a modest positive, though form has been patchy.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lion
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this William Haggas three-year-old who carries a tongue-tie flag; form figures of 7-9-6 are modest but the trainer's recent 14-day strike rate (5/28) is consistent, and this horse's running style suits a late-run race if the pace is honest enough to create a gap.

runners_data.name: Filly Eilish
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the mount for Ivan Furtado on a filly who has finished second and third from hold-up positions and shown she stays further than today's mile; three of four sim-going runs returned a placing and she represents one of the stronger closer profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Cobalt Comet
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald partners this John Mackie colt who won at 8f on Good and has a headgear flag; a genuine prominent-style horse with natural position close to Thisonesforyou, and his recent Southwell form (3rd, 3rd in sim-going) gives him clear course-and-distance credentials to challenge from the front of the chasing pack.

runners_data.name: Telfy Boy
runners_data.note: Martin Dunne's gelding returns from a huge 277-day absence with an unknown style flag, making him deeply unpredictable; two of five sim-going runs returned placings and the trip is not a concern, but the layoff is a major barrier and any market confidence would be worth noting.

runners_data.name: Alkaios
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's gelding carries the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag and has finished ninth in both recent Southwell starts, with the redistribution to midfield on the map concealing a true hold-up profile; difficult to make a case for given the form and the congested closing profile in this field.

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's colt arrives in career-best form with back-to-back wins at 8f on Good, and the trainer's remarkable 14-day hit rate (8/86) signals continued momentum; naturally prominent, only 11 days since his last run, and ideally drawn to press or track Thisonesforyou — one of the most dangerous profiles in the race from a pace-shape perspective.

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's colt has a pace flag (hg:p) and placed second at 7f on Standard going, suggesting he handles similar conditions; the redistribution to midfield reflects true closer tendencies in a crowded rear-division, but his most recent sim-going record (3/5 runs placing) is better than his Southwell finishing positions suggest.

races.paceDynamic: Thisonesforyou is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates on Southwell's flat fibresand circuit. Cobalt Comet and Hatamoto are the only other prominent-style horses, meaning the pace is unlikely to be pressured early and the tempo will be dictated entirely by Thisonesforyou and her connections. Behind her, the bulk of the field — Topathemorning, Sagremor, Venetian Lion, Filly Eilish and the rest — are true hold-up types who will be forced into a mass rearguard action, creating a bunched mid-to-late race scenario where winning runs may be cramped. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear; Kiani King, Mehmas Engine, Bosom Pals, Back At One, Alkaios and Medyg are all genuine closers who will be competing for the same ground late, and those unable to find a clean passage will be compromised. This race shape — a lone, unhurried front-runner with a wall of closers chasing — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just off the pace and pounce when the tempo is honest but not brutal: Cobalt Comet and Hatamoto are best placed to exploit that position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Pacer Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Thisonesforyou dictates a measured gallop and the prominent pair Cobalt Comet and Hatamoto track her cleanly without cover pressure.
scenarios.body: Thisonesforyou sets a sustainable rhythm, the hold-up pack is strung out chasing a deficit they cannot fully bridge, and the horses travelling closest to the pace have first run into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Cobalt Comet and Hatamoto press Thisonesforyou from the first furlong, raising the tempo enough to stretch the hold-up brigade beyond recovery range.
scenarios.body: A competitive early gallop develops across the front three, burning off the closers, and the race resolves between horses who have been on or near the pace throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp The Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner fades in the final two furlongs and a cluster of hold-up types arrive simultaneously from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A wall of hold-up horses converge on the leaders at the furlong pole, producing a blanket finish where those who find daylight earliest prevail; Topathemorning, Venetian Lion and Filly Eilish are best positioned among the closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic-Marred Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed hold-up pack suffers severe interference entering the straight, opening the door for an unconsidered horse to steal through late.
scenarios.body: The race breaks down into a messy cavalry charge, with genuine hold-up types blocked or switched wide at cost; a runner who secures a rails run early in the straight benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Hatamoto arrives on a win-win-place streak with the in-form Easterby yard firing, and his prominent style puts him in the perfect position to exploit Thisonesforyou's controlled pace — the most threatening profile in the race shape.

The hold-up cluster of Kiani King, Mehmas Engine, Bosom Pals, Back At One and Alkaios will be queuing for the same ground in the final two furlongs — watch for serious traffic issues on the bend into the straight.

Thisonesforyou has a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 suggesting she is being asked to race more prominently than ideal; if she is restrained or settles slower than expected, the pace advantage collapses entirely and the closers benefit.

Telfy Boy returns from 277 days off with an unknown tactical profile — watch for unusual market moves or a jockey booking that signals the yard believes the horse is ready, as it would be a significant flag given the extended layoff.

Cobalt Comet's headgear and prominent style make him the second-most naturally advantaged horse in this race shape; if he travels fluently in second or third, he is the likeliest to press and potentially collar Thisonesforyou before the closers arrive.

races.name: Prestige Safety Your Competent H&S Service Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Prestige Safety Construction Safety Specialists Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Bloodsweatandtyres
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a win and two places from four runs on Standard going, the most relevant surface profile here; Ben Robinson and Brian Ellison a capable combination, but 30 days fresh and will need a genuine pace to chase down — the controlled gallop Storm Free is likely to set is not ideal.

runners_data.name: Asteverdi
runners_data.note: Luke Morris rides a hold-up performer who has been operating at longer trips on soft ground recently — the drop to 7f on flat Standard Fibresand is a significant profile shift, and 52 days off adds a fitness query; James Owen's yard has been firing at 37% over 14 days which is some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Tropez Power
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type whose recent form figures of 8-8-6-6-5 on good ground tell their own story — zero wins or places from 15 runs on similar going is a damning stat, and Jack Garritty's booking does not compensate for that form line.

runners_data.name: Peter The Wolf
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose two runs at Southwell have both been on Standard going — a win over 6f and a 7th — and whose sole career win came here, which is relevant; Edward Greatrex teams up with his father Warren, and the drop back to this track could unlock something, but recent form over 5-6f on soft is patchy.

runners_data.name: Storm Free
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner in this field and able to set the terms entirely unchallenged, which is a significant tactical advantage; Hector Crouch rides for James Tate, and while the OR of 86 makes him the top-rated runner, the [STYLE_FIT] flag notes he is racing out of role in this configuration and his recent form figures of 6-19-6-1-2 show he is better on good ground — Standard AW at Southwell is the mild concern.

runners_data.name: Breakdancer
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with two wins and two places from five runs at this Southwell Standard trip profile — Silvestre De Sousa is an upgrade in the saddle and Simon & Ed Crisford are operating at a 19% 14-day strike rate; consistent form figures suggest he can hit the frame wherever he ends up in the early stages.

runners_data.name: Chalk Mountain
runners_data.note: Prominent type with two wins at Southwell specifically and a strong record on Standard going — headgear noted (hg:t, tongue tie), and just 17 days since last run suggests freshness; Alfie Redman's 7lb claim reduces the weight burden and Zoe Hawkins's yard has a small but focused operation here.

runners_data.name: City Of Kings
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has not won since a 7f victory on good ground, with a lengthy absence and a recent AW run that ended in an 11th; Sean Bowen takes the ride but Ian Williams's yard has a quiet 14-day record, and the form figure of 516/0 does not inspire confidence in this company.

runners_data.name: Ash Wednesday
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent by inclination — this is a horse with six wins and eight places from fifteen runs on Standard AW, an outstanding stat — but Daniel Muscutt rides a runner that has been pushed into a midfield mapping because the field is front-loaded with similar types; 88 days off is the significant flag, and a first run back after a long absence against horses racing in their natural positions is a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Spaceman
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent runner whose two AW starts both produced places on Standard going — a compact, positive profile for a young horse stepping to 7f; Oisin Orr is a smart booking and Richard & Peter Fahey have a live 14-day record, but the very short formbook (only three career runs) means there is genuine unknown quantity here.

runners_data.name: Lucky Luna
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose last three runs include a 7f win on soft, a 6th on good, and a 4th — she has been pushed back to a midfield mapping simply because this field is congested with pace types; Sean Levey is a quality booking for Richard Hannon, but the true test is whether she can hold a forward position without doing too much work against genuine front-runners.

runners_data.name: Exotic Baby
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by inclination who has been mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear — Jack Doughty rides for George Boughey, a yard with a 26% 14-day strike rate; one win from nine career runs and modest form figures on AW suggest she needs everything to go right, and not racing in her natural late-closing role only complicates matters further.

races.paceDynamic: Storm Free is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to dictate at a sustainable, controlled gallop from the front on Standard Fibresand at Southwell over 7f. Breakdancer, Chalk Mountain, City Of Kings, and Spaceman will press forward into prominent positions just behind, creating a compact early cluster rather than a truly pressured pace — this is a race where the tempo is set by one horse, not contested. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Lucky Luna and Ash Wednesday are true front-runners remapped to midfield, while Exotic Baby is a genuine hold-up horse also displaced; Storm Free and Breakdancer are most likely to actually secure the prominent spots they need. With one horse able to control fractions and the Southwell flat track rewarding those who travel handy, this race shape firmly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace, particularly those with proven Standard-going form here — hold-up horses face an additional burden in making up ground without the benefit of a truly searching pace to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Storm Free Controls, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Free sets an unchallenged, measured pace and the prominent hold can be sustained to the home turn.
scenarios.body: Storm Free dictates from the front at a gallop just fast enough to be sustainable, and the horses tracking him — Breakdancer, Chalk Mountain, Spaceman — find themselves perfectly positioned to pounce without having done extra work; the Standard surface at Southwell rewards this economical style especially over 7f where late closers often find the race run too steadily to make up ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Free either sets too strong a gallop under pressure from Breakdancer/Spaceman or fades inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuine contested pace develops between two or three of the prominent horses, stretching the field and creating space for horses that have settled just off the action to land late; the hold-up runners who are genuinely rearward — Bloodsweatandtyres and Tropez Power — would be the beneficiaries if the fractions are truly honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lucky Luna Creeps Into It
scenarios.trigger: If Lucky Luna (a natural prominent racer operating in a mapped midfield slot) manages to slot just behind the lead group and times her run perfectly.
scenarios.body: Being a true prominent type, Lucky Luna is unlikely to settle as far back as her mapped position suggests and may naturally drift closer to the pace in running, giving her the best of both worlds — handy enough to see the race out, fresh enough not to have led; the Richard Hannon yard and Sean Levey combination gives her a legitimate shot if she handles the step up to 7f on AW.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Field Strings Out
scenarios.trigger: If multiple remapped prominent types push forward early, creating a chaotic, high-tempo opening that strings the field out.
scenarios.body: Ash Wednesday and Lucky Luna, both natural front-runners, resist their mapped midfield roles and push up, generating a surprisingly competitive early gallop that unsettles Storm Free's rhythm and opens the race up; under this scenario horses with strong Standard-going form and proven Southwell profiles — Ash Wednesday herself and Chalk Mountain — would be best placed to exploit the mess.

watchPoints.text: Storm Free's fractions — if Breakdancer or Spaceman push forward to press him in the first two furlongs, the controlled pace evaporates and the whole shape shifts from Scenario A to Scenario B; watch the early position of those two horses at the off.

Lucky Luna and Ash Wednesday at the start — both are natural prominent types mapped to midfield, and if either rushes up to dispute early, it will create the chaotic multi-way pace scenario (Scenario D) that changes the probability landscape dramatically.

Chalk Mountain's tongue-tie and fresh angle (17 days) — she has two Southwell wins and a proven Standard record, but Alfie Redman's claim and a short turnaround means she could be a big player or a non-runner in the contest if she fails to travel early.

Ash Wednesday's 88-day absence is the longest in the field — her AW record (6W/8P from 15 Standard runs) is exceptional on form, but a first run back after nearly three months against horses at peak fitness is a meaningful discount even with Daniel Muscutt in the saddle.

races.name: Prestige Safety Construction Safety Specialists Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: King Of Fury
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a course win on Standard AW; Michael Dods yard in fair form, 22 days fresh, and the pace map here is exactly what a horse of this profile needs — a real gallop to aim at late over his favoured 7f trip.

runners_data.name: Shaman Champion
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with Clive Cox — a yard that travels for these AW handicaps when confident; showed a run-style capable of settling off the pace at Southwell distances, though recent Goodwood form on Good looks below par and the surface switch back is the key question.

runners_data.name: White Crown Star
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner who naturally wants to race prominently, but with several rivals sharing that intent, he is likely to be shuffled into a midfield berth that blunts his effectiveness; best run at Southwell came when he could dominate from the front, which is a concern here.

runners_data.name: Star Of Mali
runners_data.note: Boasts an outstanding record at Southwell on Standard — two wins and four placings from six visits — and James Tate has placed him confidently; his natural prominence means he'll be competing for a position that may be crowded, but the course affinity is the single strongest form angle in this field.

runners_data.name: Cogitate
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's five-year-old carries top weight (142lbs) and a hood; best Southwell run was a second over this course and distance on Standard, and settling off the pace in a position that suits a horse of his profile is a realistic outcome if the early rush is avoided.

runners_data.name: Eminency
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with a hood and hood/tongue-tie combination; Stuart Williams sends him here 51 days fresh, and while he controls the tempo, the STYLE_FIT flag notes he's unlikely to win a race that becomes a test of pure pace from the front — his role is as shaper, not necessarily winner.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's four-year-old has a win at Goodwood to his name and a tongue-tie fitted; naturally prominent, but this field means he's likely outgunned for the early positions — his best recent runs have come when able to travel close to the pace rather than from deep, and the redistribution genuinely compromises his chances.

runners_data.name: Comic Hero
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old has a Southwell win on Standard in his locker and PJ McDonald takes the ride — a strong tactical pairing; he wants to be prominent but may be crowded early, and his winning run here came when he found a clear pitch, making a clean start crucial.

runners_data.name: Feel The Need
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse mapped honestly here; his Standard form shows one placing from 15 tries, and recent record includes a string of double-figure finishes at Goodwood that does not inspire confidence — the redistribution tag is secondary to a form profile that is simply below the level required at present.

runners_data.name: Chale Chalo
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's three-year-old with Tom Marquand up has a Southwell win on Standard and places at this track; a natural hold-up horse who gets an ideal pace scenario, though a hood is worn and he has been beaten off in a couple of recent efforts when the race unfolded too slowly — honest pace here suits him well.

runners_data.name: Korbut
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old is only 10 days since his last run and has an extraordinary placed record at Southwell Standard — three seconds and a fifth from five visits, all on this going, all at 7f; Luke Morris rides a horse that finds the right position naturally and whose consistency in this specific context marks it as a key player in the hold-up scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Eminency is the confirmed front-runner and, crucially, is likely to be uncontested at the head of affairs — a significant tactical advantage over 7f at Southwell on a Standard AW surface that rewards horses able to dictate their own rhythm. With Eminency controlling tempo from the front, this shapes as a genuine gallop rather than a dawdle, but one set by a single horse without rivals breathing down its neck, meaning the pace is honest rather than suicidal. The field holds more prominent-minded types than can all secure their preferred position: Padua, White Crown Star, Star Of Mali, and Comic Hero are all genuine front-of-race horses who will be shuffled back into a midfield role they do not naturally favour, compressing the race shape and potentially creating a wall of horses racing out of position in the middle portions. This dynamic strongly favours the true hold-up horses — King Of Fury, Chale Chalo, and Korbut — who will find a legitimate pace to aim at and a clear late run, along with any prominent horse (Cogitate, Shaman Champion) disciplined enough to settle just off the pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eminency Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Eminency gets away cleanly and sets a genuine but sustainable gallop, leaving the compressed prominent pack to race uncomfortably in midfield.
scenarios.body: Eminency dictates a controlled pace that strings the field out, and the genuine hold-up horses — King Of Fury, Chale Chalo, and Korbut — find clear daylight to pick up in the final two furlongs against rivals that have burned energy racing out of position. This is the dominant scenario given the redistribution of several prominent types who will struggle to find their natural rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Settler Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the better-travelling prominent horses — Cogitate or Shaman Champion — settles efficiently just off Eminency and pounces entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Cogitate or Shaman Champion tracks the pace comfortably in second or third, avoids the scrimmage of redistributed prominence-seekers, and has enough left to reel in Eminency close home. This shape rewards the horse with the best combination of tactical speed and stamina who can make use of being naturally suited to a position just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Eminency sets too strong a gallop under pressure from one of the redistributed prominent types forcing their way forward early.
scenarios.body: A genuine overcooked pace sees the front end fold inside the final furlong, opening the door for the truest hold-up runners — Korbut and Chale Chalo — to sweep past a field that has overexerted itself. Korbut's consistent placed form on this course and distance at Standard going makes it the prime beneficiary if the pace genuinely blows up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Muddled Result
scenarios.trigger: If the group of redistributed prominent horses — Padua, White Crown Star, Star Of Mali — all push forward and create a contested early pace that fragments the field into several groups.
scenarios.body: The race becomes messy, with few horses settling into comfortable positions, and the winner emerges from the chaos rather than a clear tactical shape — Star Of Mali's strong course record at Southwell Standard gives it a narrow edge in this unlikely scenario. This outcome is heavily discounted because it depends on multiple horses successfully racing against their redistributed position, which the pace map suggests is improbable.

watchPoints.text: Korbut has been placed in three of his last four starts at exactly this course, distance and going combination — if he reproduces that form he is the most dangerous hold-up threat to any scenario that doesn't account for his consistency.

Star Of Mali's Southwell record (two wins, four placings from six Standard runs) is the strongest course-specific form angle in the race and should not be discounted even though he'll be racing out of his preferred prominent position.

Watch the first furlong closely for how many of Padua, White Crown Star, and Star Of Mali press forward — if two or more force their way up to challenge Eminency, the pace dynamic shifts from controlled to contested and the race shape changes materially.

Cogitate's 142lbs top weight is the highest in the field by 7lbs — if that burden tells late, horses tracking him who looked beaten may re-emerge, and it is worth watching where he is relative to the leaders at the two-furlong pole.

Comic Hero's Southwell win came from a prominent position he was able to secure cleanly — PJ McDonald's draw management and early positioning in the first 100 yards is worth monitoring given the crowd of prominent-minded rivals he'll need to navigate.

races.name: Prestige Safety Services PPE And Workwear Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bright
runners_data.note: Last-run winner over this course and trip on Standard going (1/6f/STA) is the standout flag; hold-up style means he needs a strong pace to deliver but his 6f Southwell form is the most relevant in the field.

runners_data.name: Irish Nectar
runners_data.note: Modest recent form including a 9th on Standard last time; genuine hold-up runner who needs a strong gallop to close, but has only one placed effort from six runs on similar going — limited confidence.

runners_data.name: Hierarchy
runners_data.note: Three placed efforts from twelve Standard-going runs gives a clear profile; William Carver rides and the horse has shown willingness to hit the frame, but consistent failure to win is a concern even if he gets a good run from the rear.

runners_data.name: D Flawless
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Standard (1/6f/STA) in recent form and trainer Paul Midgley is solid in these company handicaps; naturally a hold-up horse who has been pushed into the midfield map — his chance is best served if traffic clears, but he may not get the deep position he needs.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: Won at Southwell on Standard (1/6f/STA) two runs back and has course-and-distance form; though mapped to midfield here because the field is overloaded with closers, she is a true hold-up type who needs a hot pace — only two qualified runners from fifteen suggest Standard going is not her strongest suit.

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is an upgrade, but five runs without a win on Standard going and a best effort of fourth is uninspiring; a genuine hold-up horse shuffled into midfield by field composition, making his route to the winner's enclosure complicated in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Not Me
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Soft and is dropping back to 6f on a different surface; the trip and surface combination look against him, and as a hold-up type mapped out of his natural position, the race shape offers him little.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Returning from 51 days off wearing a tongue-tie; his best recent form has come over 6-7f on Good ground rather than Standard, and his hold-up style pushed to midfield here makes it hard to construct a winning scenario.

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Twice placed over 6f at Goodwood (2/6f/GOO) but only 12th at Southwell on Standard — course form is a direct concern; a hold-up horse in the congested midfield, David Nolan is capable but the horse's profile points elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard (1/7f/STA) and has three placed efforts on similar going — trip shortening to 6f could catch him out; a hold-up type forced wide in the field map, but Josephine Gordon's experience in big-field handicaps is relevant if he gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Liosa
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who won over 6f at Goodwood (1/6f/GOO) and has the course-and-trip profile to track the pace under Hector Crouch; only 2 days since last run is a watch-point, but the style maps perfectly to this race shape.

runners_data.name: Belsito
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won over 6f at Goodwood last time out (1/6f/GOO); 53 days off with the headgear retained and Kevin Stott booked — his natural racing position just off Monsieur Kodi is the most desirable tactical berth in this race.

runners_data.name: Secret Guest
runners_data.note: Six runs without a win on Good ground recently and hold-up style; dropping back to 6f on Standard with no placed efforts from seven tries on that surface makes this a tough ask for Bryan Smart's runner.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Kodi
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; Oisin Orr should land a clean lead from the gates and the Standard Southwell surface suits his style, but the STYLE_FIT tag reminds that his best recent form has come over 7f rather than 6f — stamina reserves may be tested.

races.paceDynamic: Monsieur Kodi is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and should be able to lead from the gates under Oisin Orr, setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop over Southwell's flat fibresand 6f. Behind him, Liosa and Belsito are genuine prominent types who will push forward to sit just off the pace, giving the race a clear three-horse early shape rather than a contested burn-up. The majority of the field — Bright, Irish Nectar, Hierarchy, D Flawless, Beyond Borders, Fifty Nifty and others — are true hold-up horses, but the field is saturated with closers who cannot all find their natural rear berth, meaning several will race in an unaccustomed midfield position and may not deliver their best. With an uncontested, metronomic pace set by one horse, this race shape strongly favours the nearest prominent types who can track Monsieur Kodi before he ties up, with Liosa and Belsito ideally positioned to pounce; closers face a wall of horses and a pace unlikely to be hot enough to deliver them in time.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Monsieur Kodi Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi breaks cleanly, dictates an uncontested even gallop, and the prominent chasers cannot reel him in over 6f.
scenarios.body: With no rival able to go with him early, Monsieur Kodi conserves enough energy to repel challengers; his Standard-going figures over this course and trip support a front-running win.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If Liosa or Belsito track Monsieur Kodi closely and produce a sustained drive from 2f out to collar him near the line.
scenarios.body: The tempo set by one lone front-runner is unlikely to be brutal enough to stop a well-positioned prominent horse grinding past; Belsito's recent winning form and Liosa's 6f course figures make both live threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Flies Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi goes overly fast from the front, stringing the field out and leaving a gap for the deepest closers to exploit.
scenarios.body: A genuinely quick pace would suit Bright (sole winner on Standard at Southwell in recent form) or Hierarchy (placed three times on similar going), both capable of finishing fast; however this shape requires conditions that are not the base case given one lone front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Mid-Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield causes traffic problems and a race breaks up in sections, allowing an unexposed or lightly-raced horse to emerge from the shuffle.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up horses forced into midfield, a horse like Pickersgill or Cairdeas — who can act on Standard and are less well-known quantities — could benefit from a messy race run to no one's advantage; this is the lowest-probability shape as it requires multiple misfortunes elsewhere.

watchPoints.text: Liosa ran just two days ago — monitor market moves and any late scratchings; if fresh enough, her prominent style is perfectly placed to ambush a lone leader.
Monsieur Kodi's draw and gate break are crucial — if he is slow away or bumped, the entire race shape collapses and the scenario probabilities shift sharply toward the prominent pair.

The midfield is packed with genuine hold-up horses (Fifty Nifty, D Flawless, Beyond Borders, Bright) who have all been pushed out of their natural positions — watch for traffic incidents and hard-luck stories at the 2f pole where the field will concertina.
Belsito returns from 53 days off; if the layoff shows in his early racing manners and he fails to track Monsieur Kodi promptly, his prime tactical advantage evaporates.
Trainer Paul Midgley saddles two runners (D Flawless and Cairdeas) — watch which one receives the stronger market support as an indicator of stable confidence.
